newsitem.title: SPAIN: PESETA LOSES GROUND AS MARK FIRMS ON CROSSES.
newsitem.headline: PESETA LOSES GROUND AS MARK FIRMS ON CROSSES.

text.p: The peseta lost ground in early trade on Wednesday as the mark strengthened on the crosses after the Bundesbank's cautionary note on inflation, dealers said.

"The mark rose today after the Bundesbank warned in its report that price rises had accelerated in recent months," a trader said, adding that the report sparked worries a German rate rise may be imminent.
"The Bundesbank will orientate its policy in such a way that price stability, which has been essentially achieved, can be maintained," the Bundesbank said in its August monthly report.
"The Bundesbank will observe further currency developments closely with a view to the risks presented for price stability," it said.
The dollar has gained more than 20 percent versus the mark this year.
"The market that suffered most from the comments was bonds, but it has also hit the currency market," the trader said.
German rate worries overshadowed Spain's July inflation data, which had little market impact.
July consumer prices rose 0.2 percent and 1.6 percent year-on-year, as expected. Both figures were unchanged from June.
But core prices raised eyebrows, climbing to two percent from 1.9 percent in June.
"The overall index rose 0.2 percent, which was completely discounted, and the core rate behaved worse than expected, but that did not effect the peseta," a dealer said.
At 0900 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.51/53 after 84.40/43 in early trade and 84.38/40 in late trade on Tuesday.
